description: Astatine is a chemical element with symbol At and atomic number 85. It is the rarest naturally occurring element in the Earth's crust, occurring only as the decay product of heavier elements. All of astatine's isotopes are short-lived, with the most stable being astatine-210 with a half-life of 8.1 hours.
uses: Astatine-211 is medically useful and astatine is capable of acting as a metal in antibody radiolabeling. It has been studied for its various chemical properties and compounds, though practical applications are limited by its extreme radioactivity and short half-life.
characteristics: Astatine is extremely radioactive with all isotopes having half-lives of 8.1 hours or less. It is likely to have a dark or lustrous appearance and may be a semiconductor or possibly a metal. Chemically, it displays both nonmetallic characteristics similar to iodine and some metallic behavior similar to silver, with an electronegativity of 2.2 on the revised Pauling scale.
